title: Chapter 73
content:
"Alone? Without Park Tae-soo?"

Hearing Secretary Kim’s report, Chairman Kang’s eyes narrowed into calculating, reptilian slits. Sending Seok-joo had paid off—the boy had overheard the estate guards talking. Whether completely verified or not, the takeaway was clear: Kang Il-hyun was operating entirely on his own.

For him to move without Tae-soo shadowing his heels was virtually unprecedented. On top of that, every trace of Lee Ja-kyeong had vanished into thin air. Given Il-hyun's vindictive nature, if the two had crossed paths, he never would have let the boy breathe another day. If he had kept him alive, there was only one possible reason.

"Comb through every property registered under President Kang’s name. He couldn't have gone far."

"Understood, sir."

A cold, lethal glint sharpened the Chairman's gaze. "Once you pinpoint the location, send our best people."

Secretary Kim bowed, understanding the unspoken order immediately.

Left alone, Chairman Kang leaned back against the leather cushions, a bitter, humorless smile touching his lips. Outsiders would point fingers, calling him a monster for putting a target on his own son's back just to protect his empire, but the world was rarely kind.

Father and son were cut from the exact same cloth. Unless one of them ended up in a pine box first, this war would never truly end.
Taking a single bite of the fried rice Kang Il-hyun had proudly served, Jakyeong sat in stunned silence.

After violently hacking at the onions while cursing a blue streak, had the man channeled all his tears straight into the pan? The dish was absurdly, violently salty. Fearing a full-blown tantrum if he spat it out, Jakyeong chewed slowly, glancing up at the chef across the table.

Sure enough, Il-hyun’s face fell into a grim scowl after his first mouthful, immediately chasing it with half a glass of cold water.

"Fuck. Why does it taste like this?"

Because you made it, you idiot.

Swallowing the sarcastic retort, Jakyeong watched as Il-hyun snatched both plates from the table and dumped the food straight into the stainless-steel sink. The towering man braced both hands against the counter, letting out a long, defeated sigh. Watching his broad shoulders droop, Jakyeong felt an involuntary smirk tug at his lips.

Making such a life-or-death tragedy out of a single ruined plate. And because of the man's height, his head practically brushed the upper cabinetry.

Jakyeong pushed his chair back, walked over to the double-door refrigerator, and pulled out whatever fresh ingredients he could find. When he brought them to the prep island, Il-hyun turned to watch.

"Is there any leftover rice?"

Il-hyun gave a meek nod. Checking the cooker, Jakyeong found enough steamed rice to feed an entire garrison. At least he managed to get the water ratio right.

As Jakyeong began dicing vegetables, a heavy presence stepped up behind him. Warm, solid arms wrapped around his waist, pulling him back against a broad chest.

"Making something for me yourself, darling?"

The moment hot lips grazed the sensitive curve of his neck, Jakyeong bristled, throwing his shoulder back to break the contact. When the man continued to hover and cling, Jakyeong leveled the chef's knife he was holding.

"I have a knife in my hand."

Il-hyun didn't bat an eye at the blade, but the moment Jakyeong pulled a fresh yellow onion from the basket, the corporate heir scowled and took two hurried steps back. The onion was pungent, sure, but hardly worthy of a tactical retreat.

If I’d known this a year ago, I wouldn't have bothered with sniper rounds—I would've just smothered you in chopped onions.

"Look at that technique. You're leagues better than me."

Leaning against the counter with his arms crossed, Il-hyun watched Jakyeong's movements with quiet fascination. When Jakyeong drizzled sesame oil and tossed the diced vegetables in the wok with effortless wrist flicks, Il-hyun let out a soft murmur of appreciation, offering a light, rhythmic clap.

Puffed up with pride, Jakyeong worked the pan with even greater flair—only to freeze when he caught himself putting on a performance for this lunatic.

He glanced over with a sharp scowl, finding Il-hyun grinning like a satisfied cat. I walked right into that.

Dividing the freshly tossed fried rice onto two clean plates, Jakyeong set them on the dining table.

"Let's eat," Il-hyun said, pulling out his chair. He scooped up a heaping spoonful, chewing thoughtfully before nodding in genuine approval. "Incredible. You could easily marry into my family with skills like this."

"Shut your mouth and eat."

Starting an argument was a waste of energy; deflecting the man's nonsense was an everyday chore by now.

Yet dining alone with him in a secluded villa felt intensely bizarre. With no senior housekeeper, no armed security detail, and neither Wang Han nor Wang Ryun around, the quiet intimacy was suffocating. Jakyeong kept his head down, focusing strictly on his plate.

"Care for a walk along the shore after lunch?"

"No."

"How about sex, then?"

Jakyeong glared with pure hostility, prompting a deep, amused chuckle from across the table.

"You have no idea how hard my cock gets every time you look at me with those ferocious eyes, do you?"

Remembering the grotesque discovery in his bedroom, Jakyeong sneered, "Good for you. Go drill that silicone mannequin you had made."

"That wasn't commissioned for my pleasure," Il-hyun countered, his tone turning dark and velvety. "That was a gift for you."

When Jakyeong arched a brow in question, Il-hyun flashed a cold, predatory smirk.

"A subtle reminder that if you run away again, I won't stop at an artificial mold."

A chill ran down Jakyeong's spine. He quickly looked down, shoveling rice into his mouth while pretending not to hear. The threat carried too much weight to dismiss as hyperbole—Kang Il-hyun was entirely capable of carrying it out.

After lunch, Il-hyun insisted on clearing the table and handling the dishes himself. Feeling uneasy, Jakyeong offered to wash the plates, only to be firmly escorted back to the dining chair.

"Sit right there and admire my broad back."

The sheer, shameless arrogance of it.

Il-hyun rolled his sleeves up his forearms, scrubbing the porcelain under running water. Why the man insisted on wearing a crisp, tailored dress shirt on a remote island was a mystery, but every time he leaned over the sink, the taut fabric strained across his muscular shoulders, framing the chiseled contours of his spine.

Scrubbing with excessive, heavy-handed force, he applied too much pressure, shattering a crystal glass right in his grip.

Muttering a vicious curse, he tossed the broken shards into the wastebin.

Watching from his seat, Jakyeong glanced around the open-concept villa. The quiet was almost eerie. He half-expected an armed squad to breach the perimeter at any second, but the house remained dead still, filled only by the rush of running water and the clatter of plates. The domestic rhythm was intensely disorienting.

Finished with the dishes, Il-hyun wiped his hands on a linen towel and walked over. The front of his dress shirt was soaked with water from his chaotic scrubbing.

As Il-hyun frowned down at the damp fabric, Jakyeong casually tossed out a thought:

"If you're this hopeless, you should have just brought a maid."

Il-hyun didn't answer right away, unbuttoning his shirt from the collar down.

"I hate having other people around. I wanted your undivided attention completely on me."

"..."

"I want you to use this time to take an honest look at your feelings."

"..."

"And until you're ready, I'm willing to wait."

Jakyeong frowned. "What is that supposed to mean?"

"It means while we're on this island, I won't lay a finger on you first. I give you my word. Unless, of course, you march into my bedroom and strip off your own clothes—then all bets are off."

"Keep dreaming."

The response was dry, but the man's demeanor carried an unexpected, grounded sincerity.

Kang Il-hyun was an absolute enigma. One minute he was a petulant child, the next a composed gentleman, and the next a bloodthirsty psychopath. Nailing down which mask was the real man felt impossible.

While Jakyeong was staring, Il-hyun peeled the soaked shirt completely off his shoulders, letting it drop to the floor. Then his hands dropped to his belt buckle.

Jakyeong snapped out of his daze, his expression hardening. "Why are you taking off your pants out here?"

"Taking a shower."

"Go inside the bathroom and strip!"

Ignoring the protest, Il-hyun shoved his trousers and briefs down in one fluid motion.

His thick, fully engorged erection sprang free, standing rigid and straining upward against his lower stomach. Jakyeong stared, his jaw practically hitting the floor.

Is the bastard on daily enhancement drugs? How is it standing at full mast every single time he strips?

Jakyeong whipped his head away in visceral disgust. Il-hyun kicked his clothes aside, asking smoothly:

"Want some?"

"Get the fuck out of here!" Jakyeong roared.

Il-hyun broke into a low, rumbling laugh. "I was offering dessert. There's a decent seaside café on the far tip of the island."

"..."

"We'll drive over tomorrow."

Hearing there was a commercial café on the island brought a faint wave of relief; Jakyeong had assumed they were stranded in total isolation. If there were resorts and local bistros nearby, at least they wouldn't have to rely on Il-hyun’s catastrophic cooking.

Once the bathroom door clicked shut, Jakyeong slumped back against the chair, rubbing his tired eyes.

A moment later, Il-hyun’s muffled shout echoed from the shower:

"Darling! I can't find the shampoo! Come in and help me look!"

Jakyeong didn't even turn his head, screaming at the top of his lungs:

"Stop trying your cheap tricks!"

A burst of laughter answered through the frosted glass.

Shaking his head in exasperation, Jakyeong retreated to his guest suite, locking the deadbolt securely. Turning around, he caught sight of the life-sized silicone replica standing by the window and flinched.

God, that thing is terrifying.

He grabbed a spare linen sheet from the wardrobe, draping it over the mannequin like a dust cover. Much better.

What possessed someone to fabricate a life-sized anatomical clone of another person was beyond him. And if you were going to cast it, you could've at least given it a more generous mold. Mine isn't that small. Arrogant bastard thinks everyone else is tiny just because he's built like a horse.

Fuming with petty irritation, he slipped into the master bath.

He lit a cigarette, took a few deep drags, and stripped down for a steaming shower. The hot water washed away the lingering stiffness in his muscles, leaving him feeling human again.

Stepping out, he grabbed a plush bath towel, drying off in front of the full-length vanity mirror.

Turning to check the bruises on his back, his breath caught in his throat.

There was something on his skin that hadn't been there before.

His eyes widened in sheer disbelief.

Branded neatly right across the dimple above his right hip was a line of crisp, dark lettering.

It was an English script—small, delicate, and undeniably legible:

Kang Il-hyun.

Did the bastard draw on me with a marker?

Jakyeong scrubbed the area with hot water and heavy soap, but the dark ink remained pristine and sharp beneath the suds.

It was a permanent tattoo.

Staring at the black lettering in the mirror, Jakyeong’s face twisted into an expression of pure, murderous rage.

You psychotic son of a bitch.

Throwing a dark terrycloth robe over his shoulders, he marched down the hallway on heavy, furious strides.

BAM!

He kicked the door to the master bedroom open with concussive force.

Inside, Kang Il-hyun was lounging on the edge of the mattress with a towel wrapped around his hips, a cigarette clamped between his teeth as he spoke on his burner phone.

"I'll call you back," Il-hyun said, ending the call. He looked up, arching a single dark brow. "What's the emergency?"

Jakyeong trembled with fury, pointing an accusing finger straight at his face.

"Who the fuck gave you permission to ink your name onto my body?!"

Il-hyun set the phone onto the nightstand and rose to his feet, closing the distance with slow, measured steps. The dangerous, hooded glint in his dark eyes signaled his predatory instincts taking over.

Jakyeong balled his fists. His strength had returned; in a close-quarters brawl, he was confident he wouldn't be easily overpowered.

Il-hyun tilted his head with a look of innocent confusion. "I have no idea what you're referring to."

Losing his temper completely, Jakyeong yanked the robe off his shoulders, turning to expose his lower back and hip.

"Look at this! You're telling me you don't know what this is?!"

Before the sentence fully left his mouth, a large, heavy hand clamped onto his shoulder, yanking him backward.

Jakyeong’s balance broke, his back crashing down onto the king-sized mattress with Il-hyun pinning him beneath his weight.

Trapped beneath the towering frame, Jakyeong scowled, ready to throw a punch—only to freeze.

Il-hyun reached down, effortlessly unraveling the towel from his waist with a radiant, victorious grin.

"You're the one who walked into my bedroom... and you're the one who stripped."
